items.title: Last Seen
items.reason: A six-episode missing-child mystery thriller whose complete season is now available. The story repeatedly converts uncertainty into consequential answers rather than merely extending an investigation: Ian's emergency call reopens the eleven-year disappearance; physical evidence and Donnie's lies tighten the connection to Sarah; episode 4 confirms Sarah is Maggie and turns the mystery into a rescue crisis; episode 5 reveals Henry and Jenna's history and that Henry abducted Maggie to replace their dead daughter; the finale resolves the pursuit while leaving the identity/family consequences to land emotionally. Reviews disagree on predictability and pacing, which is reflected below: the mystery and investigation are strong, but revelation cadence is not treated as constant, and the penultimate flashback slows forward motion. The Guardian calls it propulsive and says its twists matter because of their consequences; RogerEbert notes that the central truth becomes fairly easy to anticipate; other reviews flag middle-episode sag and substantial family drama. Strong fit for mystery, investigation, suspense, deception and progressive answers, with meaningful drama-focus and only moderate clue-puzzling because the audience is not solving a dense formal puzzle.
